title: Round heads: ف ق

bigIdea.text: ف (fa) and ق (qaf) share a small round head. One dot above = fa, said with the lip and teeth. Two dots above = qaf, a deep, heavy 'q' from the back of the tongue.

proper.text: Both have a small round head. ف has one dot above, ق has two. Standing alone or at the end of a word, ف has a flatter, boat-like tail and ق a deeper, round bowl. At the start or in the middle of a word only the head is left, so count the dots.

Sounds: ف is 'f' as in 'fun': the lower lip lightly touches the edges of the upper front teeth. ق is a deep, heavy 'q': the very back of the tongue presses against the back of the roof of the mouth, near the uvula, then releases. It is not a 'k' and not a gargle.

Sifat: ف is whispered (hams: the breath flows) and soft (rakhawa). ق holds the breath back (jahr), is strong (shiddah: its sound stops fully), is raised (isti'la), and bounces with a sukun (qalqalah).

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

proper.text: Heavy or light: ق is heavy (one of the seven: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ). ف is light.

Common mistakes. English speakers: ق becomes a 'k'. Persian readers: ق is said like غ (in Persian the two sound the same). Some Urdu speakers say ق as 'k' in everyday speech. Fix: press the very back of the tongue, stop the sound fully, then release; with a sukun, add the small bounce.

points.detail: Lower lip with the edges of the upper front teeth
Back of the tongue, opposite the root of the uvula

memoryHook.text: One dot: f from the lip. Two dots: q from deep in the mouth.

extras.text: ق and ك are called the two 'uvula letters' (lahawiyyatan), because they come from near the uvula.
Many London accents say 'think' as 'fink'. In Arabic, ث (tongue at the teeth) and ف (lip on the teeth) are different letters, so keep them apart.

tip.text: ق stops: the back of the tongue presses and releases (and bounces with a sukun). غ never stops: a flowing gargle from the top of the throat, just behind qaf's place. Persian readers: this is your pair.
ف: the lower lip touches the upper front teeth. ث: the tongue tip meets the edges of the upper front teeth, and the lips stay apart.

remnote: ف (fa) == Round head, one dot above; lower lip with the edges of the upper front teeth; 'f'; light
ق (qaf) == Round head, two dots above; back of the tongue near the uvula; deep 'q' that stops; heavy; bounces with sukun
Fix for ق == Not 'k' and not a gargle: stop deep at the back of the tongue, then release
London 'fink' habit == Keep ث (tongue at the teeth) apart from ف (lip on the teeth)
